Hi Alice — quick technical summary below, happy to expand in a call.

PHI handling (short):
- Inference path: customer data submitted to Redwood endpoints is accepted into the request pipeline, processed in-memory for tokenization and model execution, and results returned. The default hosted offering does not persist raw input by default; we provide options.
- Logs & metrics: by default we collect minimal request metadata (timestamp, model variant, latency, token counts). Content-level logging is off for customers unless explicitly enabled for debugging; when enabled, content logs are encrypted at rest and access-controlled.
- KV cache: model KV cache is kept in memory for serving performance; snapshots are not persisted to disk unless a customer opts into long-lived session storage.
- Retention: for hosted customers with PHI, our standard policy is to require Dedicated deployment or a hosted plan with explicit data-processing restrictions written into the BAA (we can configure to not keep content logs and to purge monitoring payloads within an agreed SLA).
- Encryption & keys: data in transit is TLS 1.2+/1.3; at rest we use AES-256. Customers can use customer-managed keys (CMK) on Dedicated and Private deployments; for hosted we support KMS integrations for enterprise tiers.
- Subprocessors: primary compute in hosted is with a regional cloud provider (US regions only for this pilot if requested). Monitoring/telemetry vendor (LogStream Inc) has subprocessor status and is included in the BAA appendix; full list to be provided by Mina.

Recommendation for your pilot (5k US records):
- If BrightPath requires a signed BAA and prohibits any content persistence in multi-tenant environments, we recommend Dedicated capacity for the pilot to minimize operational controls and simplify audit points.
- If you accept contractual restrictions that no content is stored and logs are configured to exclude payloads, a hosted arrangement may be sufficient and faster to stand up.

Happy to schedule a 30-minute technical walkthrough to map your data flow to our controls.

Rishi
